newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SCHOLZ OUT, THOMSON IN S.AFRICA TOUR SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SCHOLZ OUT, THOMSON IN S.AFRICA TOUR SQUAD.

text.p: South Africa's rugby selectors on Thursday made two changes to the 36-player squad to tour Argentina, Wales and France, dropping centre Christiaan Scholz and prop Os du Randt because of injury.
A statement from the South African Rugby Football Union said Scholz, from Transvaal, would be replaced by Natal's Jeremy Thomson, who earns his first call-up for Springbok duty.
A replacement for Free State's du Randt is to be named on Saturday after semifinal matches in the Currie Cup domestic championship.

The selection of Thomson, a leading try scorer in a Natal team that reached the final of the Super 12 competition this year, will go some way to answering fierce criticism of the make-up of the squad to tour in November and December.
Coach Andre Markgraaff sparked a storm of protest when he dropped World Cup captain Francois Pienaar, saying his form had slumped.
He also picked three relatively obscure players from Griqualand West province which does not rank among the five strongest domestic teams.
Markgraaff was criticised for not selecting Thomson in the first place and was also taken to task for picking four loosehead props, including du Randt, and only one tighthead specialist.
